interpretation_rules: Position weight is a common multiplicative factor within DB and cannot explain DB1-versus-DB32 spacing.
The prior DL/LB transport-residual finding must not be generalized to DB without direct DB evidence.
A statistical outlier is a review signal, not proof that a named DB is mispriced.
A structural audit may identify compression, discontinuities, lineage drift, or counterfactual sensitivity but cannot choose a new DB scale or age curve.
Weeks 1-3 realized outcomes are descriptive only and cannot authorize a model change.
Production V2 Phase 1 is an uncalibrated transparent benchmark, not a validated replacement.
No named DB may be manually raised or lowered from this audit.
Any follow-up model change requires a separately preregistered broad-cohort calibration/validation study.
Kickers are excluded from the positional structural-audit series.
primary_questions: Does the live DB board reproduce the exact deployed FV formula with no hidden DB-only mutation?
How much of within-DB spacing comes from production multiplier versus age multiplier?
Does the DB upper tail contain statistically unusual FV, production-multiplier, or adjacent-rank gaps?
Do DB age anchors create sharp discontinuities or age-floor cliffs?
Do elite floors, no-history role rescue, production clamps, or age floors materially shape the DB board?
Does the transparent Production V2 benchmark materially reorder DBs or mostly preserve current ordering?
Does legacy production-multiplier lineage show unusual DB drift relative to the overall player pool?
Do frozen Weeks 1-3 outcome diagnostics support only descriptive monitoring rather than model selection?
Does current DB position weight show cross-position tension in frozen pairwise diagnostics?
Was DB isolated from the frozen DL/LB position-lineage deployment and subsequent DL/LB structural issue?
scope: All current PLAYER_DB defensive backs in the deployed calculator.
